title: Training Dataset Row
description: JSONL format for fine-tuning datasets. Each line is one JSON object matching either the SFT or DPO variant.
$comment: EVAL-GATE SEMANTICS (Pillar 3 SSOT — see adapta/training/evaluator.py, models.py). The fine-tune is gated, before it can serve, on its quality on this dataset, but the gate is built to measure GENERALIZATION, not memorization: (1) HELD-OUT SPLIT — the worker holds out the last ~20% of rows (>=1 row; adapta.training.models.split_holdout) and trains only on the rest; the gate scores ONLY the held-out rows, never rows the model trained on. (2) RESPONSE-ONLY LOSS — for SFT the score is the cross-entropy on the `response` tokens only (prompt/system masked, label -100). For DPO the gate scores the `chosen` tokens as the target response — the same loss-based metric, measuring whether the DPO-tuned model can reproduce preferred outputs. (3) score = exp(-avg_response_loss) = 1/perplexity, clamped to [0,1]. (4) THE GATE (adapta.training.models.passes_eval_gate) — an adapter is promotable if it passes EITHER path: ABSOLUTE `score >= eval_score_threshold` (default 0.6, ~perplexity 1.67), OR IMPROVEMENT — it clears a low sanity floor (`eval_min_floor`, default 0.05) AND beats the base model on the SAME held-out split by `eval_min_improvement` (default 0.05). The base (un-adapted) model is scored on the same split and the adapter-minus-base delta is reported (base_score/score_delta). The improvement path exists because a small base model cannot reach the absolute perplexity bar even on an ideal task, yet a fine-tune that reliably out-scores its base has demonstrably learned the target behavior (§A3.2). An adapter that passes neither → EvalGateFailed (HTTP 422), not registered, endpoint cannot bind it.

SFTRow.title: SFT instruction-pair row (method=sft)
SFTRow.description: Supervised fine-tuning: a prompt the model receives and the ideal response it should learn to produce.

prompt.description: The instruction or question given to the model.

response.description: The ideal response the model should produce.

images.description: §V image-understanding fine-tunes: paths RELATIVE to the dataset bundle (zip) the row's image(s) live in. Exactly 1 image per row in v1 (the array is forward-compat). Image tokens are context like prompt tokens — masked from the eval-gate's response-only loss, so the gate semantics in $comment are unchanged. Formats: png/jpg/jpeg/webp. Rows without this key are plain text rows (full back-compat).

metadata.description: Optional arbitrary metadata (source, quality score, etc.)

DPORow.title: DPO preference-pair row (method=dpo)
DPORow.description: Direct Preference Optimisation: a prompt with a preferred (chosen) and a dispreferred (rejected) completion. The model learns to assign higher probability to the chosen response.

prompt.description: The instruction or context shown to the model.

chosen.description: The preferred (better) response the model should learn to favour.

rejected.description: The dispreferred (worse) response the model should assign lower probability.

metadata.description: Optional arbitrary metadata (source, quality score, annotator, etc.)
